assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength lattice concept with Ye's realisation of Sr clocks at fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It reshaped precision measurement and opened the way to tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The idea is original, clear and has clear lasting impact. As an atomic theorist I can judge the atomic-structure side (magic wavelengths, systematic shifts) well, and I find it sound.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and demonstrated early Sr lattice spectroscopy. Ye's group drove the highest-accuracy and many-body-enhanced implementations. Other groups (for example at JILA, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, Tokyo) contributed, but the two-person configuration is defensible. The relation to the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock recognition is a framing point, not an obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Independent confirmation across many laboratories and species, with agreement at the 1e-18 level and growing deployment in international timekeeping comparisons.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize.
Credit for early lattice-clock proposals and the role of Hall and Hansch-era comb technology in the practical realisation is a point of nuance I have not verified in detail.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele proposal of the quantum spin Hall effect and the topological Z2 classification, together with its experimental realisation in HgTe wells, established topological insulators as a new class of matter. The impact on condensed-matter physics, materials and quantum-device ideas is large and lasting, and the concept builds on and extends the 2016 topological-phase prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical contribution. Molenkamp's group realised and observed the helical edge transport, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. That proposal and the 3D topological-insulator work (Moore-Balents, Fu-Kane-Mele, Hasan, Zhang and others) are not in the credited names, so any configuration leaves real credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with extensive independent confirmation of edge transport and 3D materials, although the 2D quantum spin Hall experimental signatures have remained largely confined to a few material systems.
uncertainties: Credit division between the 2D proposal, the HgTe prediction and experiment, and the 3D topological-insulator discoveries.
I am not certain how the committee will weigh the absence of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hexapole and related correctors for spherical aberration brought electron microscopy to sub-angstrom resolution and enabled atomic-resolution imaging in materials physics and chemistry. This is a clear invention whose lasting impact is evident in routine use worldwide. It is instrument physics of a kind the Nobel tradition has recognised (electron microscope, STM).
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical corrector design, Haider led the first working implementation in the Heidelberg and EMBL context, and Urban led the work in demonstrating atomic-resolution materials imaging with it. The three-person split is natural and matches the established award history of the technique. Other contributors (e.g. Krivanek, Zach) could be seen as having a claim, which I cannot settle from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent use and commercial deployment. Recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Priority and credit relative to competing aberration-correction efforts, such as the Krivanek and Zach groups.
Whether the committee treats this as primarily physics or as engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought cavity-QED strong coupling to superconducting circuits, with the Blais-Huang-Wallraff-Girvin-Schoelkopf proposal and its experimental demonstration. It underpins dispersive readout and the transmon-based quantum processors in current use. The concept is original and its influence on quantum technology and quantum-optics-style experiments is lasting. It is distinct in subject from the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, although related in hardware.
assessment.attribution: Blais gave the theoretical framework, Wallraff the first strong-coupling demonstration, and Schoelkopf's group the transmon and wider architecture work. The three-name configuration is plausible, but Girvin, Huang, Devoret and others carry substantial claims that sit outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Largely mature after twenty years of independent confirmation, though the application to computing is still in flux and the committee might find it somewhat close to the 2025 recognition of superconducting circuits.
uncertainties: Relationship to the 2025 prize and how it affects timing.
Credit for Girvin, Devoret and the transmon inventors, not supplied here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction at the magic angle and the observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene opened twistronics and a very active field of correlated 2D matter. Originality and influence are both high, and the result links a precise theoretical prediction to a striking experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental observations. The configuration is clean on the supplied names. Cao and Fatemi, as principal experimental authors, and other contributors (Dean, Yacoby, Young and others) complicate the allocation outside the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably well confirmed by many groups, but the origin of superconductivity and the full phase diagram remain debated, and the field is still evolving quickly, so some caution on timing is warranted.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated states remain contested.
Credit for early graduate-student experimenters and for related theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, and by Suarez Morell.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices, with the Jaksch-Zoller proposal of the Bose-Hubbard model and the Greiner-Bloch demonstration of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, created controllable quantum simulators for many-body physics. Quantum-gas microscopy extended this to single-site resolution. The work is original, widely applied and close to my own field of atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided the theoretical proposals, Greiner and Bloch the experiments, and Bloch the broader development of the field. Jaksch, Gardiner and Cirac and the quantum-gas-microscope groups (Greiner, Bakr, Gross and Bloch) have claims that are not all in the supplied names. A three-person prize is possible but needs care with the theory credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature in its core results and well replicated across many groups. Quantum simulation advantage claims are still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and the 2012 prize for quantum control of single systems.
Allocation between the Jaksch-Zoller theory team and the experimentalists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation solves horizon and flatness problems and, through the Mukhanov-Chibisov quantum-fluctuation mechanism, explains the near scale-invariant spectrum confirmed by CMB measurements. It is among the most consequential ideas in modern cosmology. I judge this from outside my own specialty and defer to cosmologists on the fine points.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the inflationary scenario, Linde the new and chaotic inflation, and Mukhanov the origin of structure from quantum fluctuations. Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt, Sato and Hawking all have claims, so the three-name configuration leaves meaningful credit unresolved and may be contested.
assessment.maturity: The spectrum and flatness are consistent with data, but there is no decisive confirmation such as primordial tensor modes, and alternatives are still discussed, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Absence of a direct signature such as primordial gravitational waves.
Contested priority among Guth, Linde, Starobinsky, Mukhanov, Albrecht, Steinhardt and Sato.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84, the Ekert protocol and quantum teleportation are foundational for quantum information science and quantum communication, with strong conceptual originality and widespread experimental development and deployment of QKD. They build on the physics of entanglement recognised in 2022.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear originators of BB84 and teleportation (with Crepeau, Jozsa, Peres and Wootters as co-authors of the teleportation paper), while Ekert independently proposed entanglement-based key distribution. The three-person configuration is natural for QKD but leaves teleportation co-authors outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Foundational ideas are decades old and extensively confirmed. Practical security and technology readiness remain debated, but this does not weaken the scientific achievement.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards this as physics versus computer science or information theory.
Credit for teleportation co-authors and for Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea, not in the supplied names.
